newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Harbour tunnel opens early, under budget.
newsitem.headline: HK Harbour tunnel opens early, under budget.

text.p: The third road tunnel under Hong Kong's harbour opened for business on Wednesday -- three months ahead of schedule and HK$600 million (US$77.5 million) under budget.
"The latest forecast of total project costs of HK$6.9 billion represents a saving of HK$600 million," Hong Kong Chief Secretary Anson Chan said as she declared the tunnel open.

Western Harbour Tunnel Company Ltd chairman Robert Adams said the tunnel linking Hong Kong island and Kowloon on the mainland, opened three months ahead of schedule. It can handle 180,000 vehicles a day.

The tunnel, designed to relieve some of the heavy congestion that builds up on the existing cross-harbour routes, was funded by the private sector on a build, operate, transfer basis and will revert to the government after 30 years.

The two km (1.2 mile) tunnel, one of 10 "Core Projects" associated with Hong Kong's new airport. From Kowloon an expressway connects to the new Chek Lap Kok airport, which is due to open to air traffic next year, a container port and to a new superhighway to China's southern city of Guangzhou.
The toll charge is set at HK$30, three times as much as the other two cross-harbour links.
Western Harbour Tunnel Co is 37 percent owned by the Cross-Harbour Tunnel Co Ltd and 35 percent by CITIC Pacific Ltd. (US$1=HK$7.74)
